stem: In which scenario would 'watchful waiting' NOT be recommended for a child with suspected acute otitis media?

options.text: A child under six months of age
A child over two years of age with a unilateral infection
A child with a mild upper respiratory tract infection
An adolescent with a history of swimming in chlorinated pools

explanation: Antibiotics are recommended regularly for children at risk, specifically those under six months of age.
rationale: Risk factors for immediate treatment include very young age, bilateral disease in toddlers, or underlying craniofacial anomalies.

optionExplanations.A: Antibiotics are recommended regularly for children at risk, specifically those under six months of age.
optionExplanations.B: Watchful waiting is generally appropriate for older children with infection in only one ear and no other high-risk factors.
optionExplanations.C: Most viral respiratory infections involving the ear are initially observed to see if they progress to a bacterial stage.
optionExplanations.D: This history might suggest otitis externa, but for AOM, this demographic does not automatically bypass the watchful waiting period.

source.hint: Risk factors for immediate treatment include very young age, bilateral disease in toddlers, or underlying craniofacial anomalies.
